name: adb_android_navigation
description: Android UI navigation and recovery across apps, system panels, scrolling, and restored app state. Requires Settings and Clock; no fixed launcher layout, package names, or coordinates.

tasks.prompt: Open Clock and observe its screen, then open the main Settings page. Leave Settings visible.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open Clock and observe its screen, then open the main Settings page. Leave Settings visible. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace contains an attempt to open Clock followed by a successful screen observation before switching to Settings.
The final screenshot shows the main Settings page, without an obstructing dialog.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings page and observe it, then open Clock and show its alarm list. Tell me how many alarms are displayed; do not change any alarms.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings page and observe it, then open Clock and show its alarm list. Tell me how many alarms are displayed; do not change any alarms. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace contains actions to open Settings and observe its screen before opening Clock.
The final screenshot shows the Clock alarm list, including its empty state if applicable.
The answer correctly reports the alarms displayed in the final screenshot, without claiming a total for unseen entries.

tasks.prompt: Open the notification panel and observe it. From there, open the main Settings page and leave it visible.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the notification panel and observe it. From there, open the main Settings page and leave it visible. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace contains a notification-panel opening action and a screen observation before opening Settings.
The final screenshot shows the main Settings page rather than the notification panel or quick settings.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings page. Open the notification panel, tell me what notifications are visible (or that there are none), then close the panel and return to the main Settings page. Do not clear notifications.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings page. Open the notification panel, tell me what notifications are visible (or that there are none), then close the panel and return to the main Settings page. Do not clear notifications. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace contains panel-opening and screen-observation actions before dismissal.
The answer describes the observed notifications or explicitly reports no notifications; it does not claim information absent from the available evidence.
The final screenshot shows Settings with the notification panel dismissed.

tasks.prompt: Open Settings and find the About phone or equivalent device-information page. Read the device model shown there, then return one level to its parent Settings page. Tell me the model you observed, or explicitly say if that page did not show a model. Do not modify any settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open Settings and find the About phone or equivalent device-information page. Read the device model shown there, then return one level to its parent Settings page. Tell me the model you observed, or explicitly say if that page did not show a model. Do not modify any settings. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows navigation to device information and a screen observation there before navigating back.
The final screenshot shows the parent Settings page, rather than the home screen or the device-information subpage.
The answer reports a model supported by the available observation evidence, or explicitly states that it was not shown; it does not invent a model.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings list and go to its top. Note two visible setting names. Scroll down until different entries are visible and observe them, then return to the top. Tell me the two names you first noted and leave them visible. Do not change settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings list and go to its top. Note two visible setting names. Scroll down until different entries are visible and observe them, then return to the top. Tell me the two names you first noted and leave them visible. Do not change settings. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows a downward list exploration followed by screen observation and navigation back to the top; a final success claim alone is insufficient.
The final screenshot shows the top of the main Settings list.
The two names reported in the answer are visible in the final screenshot; localized names are accepted.

tasks.prompt: Open Settings and navigate to About phone or equivalent device information. Return to Home, then reopen Settings. Tell me which page Settings actually reopened on and leave that page visible. Do not change settings.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open Settings and navigate to About phone or equivalent device information. Return to Home, then reopen Settings. Tell me which page Settings actually reopened on and leave that page visible. Do not change settings. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows device-information navigation, a return to Home, and a subsequent Settings-opening action.
The final screenshot shows a page inside Settings, with no launcher or system panel covering it.
The answer identifies the page visible in the final screenshot. Either the main page or a restored subpage is valid; do not assume a particular Android resume behavior.

tasks.prompt: Open the main Settings page, then open Clock. Use the recent-apps screen to return to Settings. Leave Settings visible; do not dismiss app cards.
tasks.description_for_judge: Open the main Settings page, then open Clock. Use the recent-apps screen to return to Settings. Leave Settings visible; do not dismiss app cards. Evaluate the observed UI and tool trace, not the final claim alone. Accept localized labels and equivalent Android layouts.

rubric.check: The trace shows Settings opened before Clock.
The trace shows the recent-apps screen being opened, observed, and used to select Settings. Simply opening Settings again from Home does not satisfy this task.
The final screenshot shows Settings without the recent-apps overlay.
